# Infusion Services

## Brown University Health Infusion Centers

For the convenience and comfort of patients here in Rhode Island and southeastern Massachusetts, we provide numerous  infusion centers to treat cancer and non-cancerous conditions. Our treatments include:

  * Chemotherapy
  * Neurology infusions
  * Iron infusions
  * Hydration
  * Blood transfusions
  * Remicade (for rheumatoid arthritis)
  * Gastrointestinal conditions (Crohn’s disease, colitis)
  * Neurology Infusions

# Raia's Chemo Treatment for Lymphoma

ImageImage

Hi, my name is Calia. I am the Operations Manager of a women-owned and operated pet service called Tails N' Trails Pets LLC. We have three branches serving Rhode Island, Worcester, MA, and Southeastern Wisconsin. One of our walkers, Kate, received some of the worst news any pet owner never wants to hear. Kate's dog, Raia, was diagnosed with lymphoma in August. She has battled and beat mast cell cancer before, too. Luckily, they caught it early on, and Raia is responding very well to chemotherapy, but they have a long road ahead to fight this battle. Kate brings Raia to Veterinary Cancer Specialists of New England in Cape Cod for chemotherapy once a week, for a total of 18 weeks. This treatment will ultimately amount to upwards of $10-12,000. Any animal lover would agree that you can't put a price tag on your family, and that's exactly what Raia is to Kate.

### Nhianh Pasierb, DVM

Originally from the Boston Area, Dr Nhianh (Annie) Pasierb attended Boston University, where she received her bachelor’s degree in both Biology and Mathematics in 2000. After graduation, she attended Tufts University School of Veterinary Medicine and received her Doctorate in 2006. She continued her education with a rotating internship at Angell Animal Medical Center in Boston. She spent the following three years on active duty as a Captain in the U.S. Army Veterinary Corps. After another year in a specialty surgical internship at Sonora Veterinary Specialist in Phoenix, AZ, she decided to move back to the New England area and joined the Newport Animal Hospital Team in December 2012.

Thankfully, the remainder of my chemotherapy treatment drastically changed when an unexpected acquaintance turned into my rock, my best friend and my biggest supporter.
Image: Amanda HanleyHanley during her cancer treatment.

Life with cancer became real when I sat down with the student services office at WPI and handed in my medical leave of absence paperwork. I would not be starting my senior year with all of my friends. I would be in Rhode Island living with my parents and commuting to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute in Boston every week to undergo chemotherapy. 

I was determined to stay on track as best as I could. I would not let cancer derail my life completely. I registered for three classes at my state school, the University of Rhode Island, for the summer and fall semesters to ensure I would not fall too far behind.

 It’s June 24, 2012, and I arrive at Dana-Farber for my first chemotherapy infusion. My parents are silent and I am numb. Everyone around me is trying their best to put on a smile and make this as positive of an experience as it can be. 

The port in my chest gets accessed for the first time and I remember tasting the saline in my mouth as it is flushed.
